sbar.situation: The bank payment journey has recovered. Two recovery checks in a row ran clean, the last at 30 s.
sbar.background: The primary fraud screening service slowed to a p95 of 1820 ms against a 15 ms baseline, so every payments call to screening timed out. The clearing worker exited with code 15 and stopped answering. A pipeline change raised the gateway balance_cache_ttl_s from 0.5 to 600.0.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander failed screening over to its standby, restarted the clearing worker and reverted the gateway balance_cache_ttl_s from 600.0 to 0.5, and all three actions completed. The slow primary screening (confidence 0.9) caused the payments and gateway failures, and the stopped clearing worker (0.85) left 18 items queued, starting with item 91, which had never been attempted. The 600 s cache (0.7) would have shown stale balances after payments completed.
sbar.recommendation: Check that payments logs now show screening calls going to the standby instead of 'via primary', and find out why the primary screening service slowed before failing back to it. Confirm that the 18 queued clearing items, starting with item 91, are processed, and find out what terminated the worker and why the pipeline set the 600 s TTL. Operations should review the payments that failed screening during the outage and any balances shown while the 600 s cache was active.
